research_conclusion: UNVERIFIED (external cost robustness). Under the existing cost model the qualified momentum edge is cost-robust on the predeclared grid: 6/6 baseline COST_ROBUST assets (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA) survive the realistic, conservative and stress levels, and median cost drag is 0.0000 (range -0.003..+0.001). But the model does not charge a genuine transaction cost: the engine applies the same additive fill price on entry and exit, so fixed slippage cancels over a completed round trip, proportional slippage scales P&L by (1+p), and fold total_return uses only within-test equity change. The AMZN full-sample diagnostic is decisive: zero +5.5373, commission-only +5.5162, slippage-only-stress +5.5460 (higher than zero), full-stress +5.5250; commission (~$21,055 over 4451 fills) is the only real cost. The result is reproducible and independently verified (5 gates MATCH, 171/171 tests), but it does not establish robustness to external transaction costs.
unverified: Cost robustness to external transaction costs is UNVERIFIED: the engine applies the same additive fill price (close + slippage_cents/100 + close*slippage_proportional) on entry and exit, so fixed slippage cancels over a completed round trip and proportional slippage multiplies both legs by (1+p); fold total_return is eq[-1]/eq[0]-1 on the test segment, so costs incurred before the test segment are excluded. Only commission is a genuine round-trip cost in the current model.
For the LEARNING_PROCESS role the selector ranks a self-audit of itself (P-001) as the top task, so the selection cannot be treated as independent evidence of improved information flow.
